errors.english: Because if the certainty of being of that nature [note: essential identity] and arising from that [note: causality] follows it
errors.why: It is the capacity to convey knowledge (gamakatva) that follows the certainty of tādātmya and tadutpatti, not the certainty that follows it.

fix.find: Because if the certainty of being of that nature [note: essential identity] and arising from that [note: causality] follows it,

errors.english: The text states: It is not a negation.
errors.why: The commentator says the refutation (of the doubt) is the root-text phrase "it is not"; 'gog pa is the subject, not part of the quoted words.

fix.find: The text states: It is not a negation.
fix.replace: The refutation is the phrase "It is not."

errors.english: Previously, this commentary was presented
errors.why: rnam 'grel here is the Pramāṇavārttika (the root verse being explained), not 'this commentary'.

fix.replace: Previously, this [verse of the] Vārttika was presented

errors.english: To this, the text says: Also for possession.
errors.why: The root-text words "also for conjunction" are where the opponent's doubt is voiced, not the text's reply to it.

errors.english: [note: original: "ldan pa", the relation of inherence or conjunction]
errors.why: ldan pa is conjunction (saṃyoga); inherence ('du ba, samavāya) is a separate relation treated next, so the note conflates them.

note: Follows the argument in outline but inverts who follows what, misreads the refutation formula and mistakes the Vārttika for 'this commentary'.

errors.english: In this way he has taught the cause of those who cling.
errors.why: With honorific mnga' ba the clinging is the Buddha's (apparent) adherence: this shows the reason why he seems to have attachment, not the cause of others' clinging.

note: A careful, faithful rendering of the elephant-gaze passage with one doubtful referent.

errors.english: The Primary Matrix is inferred through its potentiality, by showing that an effect cannot be explained otherwise; so through the very nature of vitality
errors.why: The subject is the effect posited in the pradhāna in the form of potentiality (because effects are otherwise impossible), which as the pradhāna's very life/essence is also hollow; 'vitality' and making the pradhāna the thing inferred misread it.

note: Sound rendering of the Sāṃkhya refutation; one sentence garbled.

span_why: The English opens with the sentence 'This is because even if the absence of a self is excluded, a nature characterized as a self is not positively projected' which belongs to the previous side, instead of the sentence closed by zhes at the head of this side.

errors.english: the rule that if the result is absent, the cause must be absent
errors.why: Vyatireka-vyāpti is that where the probandum is absent the reason is absent; 'result/cause' is misleading for an inference about a self.

note: The argument against the Naiyāyika 'life-breath' proof is followed accurately.
Faithful rendering of the sūtra quotation on causes of defilement and purification and the Tathāgata's absorptions.

errors.english: they become vitalized
errors.why: skyes here is 'gift': when he meets the noble his words become like a gift.

errors.english: "Proof" ends mid-word at page boundary
errors.why: An unmarked editorial remark that is not a translation of anything in the Tibetan.

errors.english: This is written from the perspective of mastering elegant speech.
errors.why: This first verse concerns skill in speech that establishes one's own position; 'well-spoken words' (legs par bshad pa) is the topic of the second verse, so 'elegant speech' conflates the two.

note: The grammatical glosses are followed, but 'like a gift' is lost and a meta-remark is left in the text.

errors.english: those beams, which individually lack the capacity to support the pillar,
errors.why: The example is of those who individually cannot lift the beam (gdung ma) but can together; the beam is what is lifted, and there is no pillar.

fix.find: those beams, which individually lack the capacity to support the pillar,
fix.replace: those who individually lack the capacity to lift the beam,

errors.english: refers to the term for a single class
errors.why: The commentator notes a grammatical point: the singular is used for the class (memory and recognition together), not 'a term for a single class'.

errors.english: is a sign established by direct perception
errors.why: The inference arises from a sign whose relation (with the inferred parts) is established by perception; the inference is not itself the sign, and 'relation' is dropped.

note: Generally follows the debate on the whole and its parts, but misreads the beam-lifting example and a few technical turns.

errors.english: If this were to change, these two would not be the same.
errors.why: The opponent says this case too would be likewise (as with the 'flowering forest'); the reply is that the two cases are not alike — nothing 'changes'.

fix.find: If this were to change, these two would not be the same.
fix.replace: If [one says] this too would be likewise: these two are not alike.

errors.english: is established by the assembly of trees that have the quality of full blooms, it would be appropriate to call it an assembly meeting in a single object
errors.why: 'du ba is the Vaiśeṣika relation of inherence (samavāya): floweringness inheres in the trees, so it can be called inherence in one object; 'assembly' destroys the argument.

fix.find: is established by the assembly of trees that have the quality of full blooms, it would be appropriate to call it an assembly meeting in a single object
fix.replace: has the quality of full bloom inhering in the trees, it would be appropriate to call it inherence in a single object

errors.english: However, as for what is explained here regarding diversity:
errors.why: The thesis that variegatedness here does not inhere in the whole in which the conjunction exists is not translated.

fix.find: However, as for what is explained here regarding diversity:
fix.replace: But here variegatedness does not inhere in the whole in which the conjunction exists; this is what is explained by:

errors.english: Well then, how is fire perceived as fire?
errors.why: ji ltar opens the opponent's simile ('just as one who has apprehended fire as fire ... superimposes fire on the brahmin boy'), not a question.

note: The Vaiśeṣika vocabulary (inherence rendered 'assembly') and the objection-reply structure are repeatedly misread at the start; the citra-cognition argument later is better.
Faithful verse rendering of the Tibetan; the interleaved Sanskrit is rightly not translated twice.

errors.english: the truth of recollection and the (Vedas) sacred scriptures
errors.why: dran pa paired with rig byed is Smṛti (the law-books), not 'recollection'.

fix.replace: the truth of the Smṛti and the (Vedas) sacred scriptures

errors.english: For those possessing steadfast, noble minds and great wisdom, encountering beings such as you is not easy to find.
errors.why: The steadfast weighty mind and great wisdom belong to 'those like you': the appearance of such great-minded ones as you is hard to find.

errors.english: Thus have I heard
errors.why: rjes su thos (anuśrūyate) is the Jātakamālā's 'thus it is handed down', not the sūtra formula evaṃ mayā śrutam.

errors.english: equal to the immortal master and teacher of the gods
errors.why: This is Bṛhaspati, the guru of the gods / of the lord of the immortals (Indra), a proper-name epithet rather than two descriptions.

note: Readable and mostly accurate verse and narrative, with a few term slips (Smṛti, Bṛhaspati, the opening formula).
